title: The Past, Present and Future of Amy Coney Barrett

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》旗下的每日通讯《Dealbook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的Dealbook峰会上，现场采访一些在商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多嘉宾。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 届时，您可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望您能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 您一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今日话题。

sentences.en: With 36 days to go until the election, Amy Coney Barrett has been nominated as the next Supreme Court Justice of the United States,
sentences.zh: 距离大选还有36天，艾米·科尼·巴雷特已被提名为下一任美国最高法院大法官，

sentences.en: and President Trump and Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell have vowed to get her confirmed before Americans go to the polls.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统和参议院多数党领袖米奇·麦康奈尔已誓言要在美国民众投票前确认她的任命。

sentences.en: My colleague, Adam Liptak, on what it all means for the court and the future of American law.
sentences.zh: 我的同事亚当·利普塔克将为您解读这对最高法院和美国法律的未来意味着什么。

sentences.en: It's Monday, September 28th.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月28日，星期一。

sentences.en: I stand before you today to fulfill one of my highest and most important duties under the United States Constitution, the nomination of a Supreme Court Justice.
sentences.zh: 我今天站在你们面前，是为了履行我在美国宪法下最高、最重要的职责之一：提名一位最高法院大法官。

sentences.en: Adam, it has happened.
sentences.zh: 亚当，这件事已经发生了。

sentences.en: And so I wonder if you can tell us about the announcement that was held over the weekend.
sentences.zh: 我想请你为我们介绍一下周末举行的那场宣布仪式。

sentences.en: So on Saturday, there was a ceremony at the Rose Garden at the White House that was in one sense ordinary.
sentences.zh: 周六，白宫玫瑰园举行了一场仪式，从某种意义上说，它是寻常的。

sentences.en: It was the announcement of a Supreme Court nominee, but in another sense, quite extraordinary, at least as a matter of timing.
sentences.zh: 那是对最高法院提名人的宣布，但从另一个角度来看，它又相当不寻常，至少在时间安排上是这样。

sentences.en: Over the past week, our nation has mourned the loss of a true American legend.
sentences.zh: 过去一周，我们国家一直在哀悼一位真正的美国传奇人物的离世。

sentences.en: Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg was a legal giant president and a pioneer for women.
sentences.zh: 露丝·巴德·金斯伯格大法官是一位法律泰斗，也是女性权益的先驱。

sentences.en: It happened just eight days after the death of Justice Ruth Bader
sentences.zh: 这件事发生在露丝·巴德·金斯伯格大法官去世仅八天后，

sentences.en: Ginsburg, and just weeks before a presidential election.
sentences.zh: 距离总统大选也仅剩几周时间。

sentences.en: So you had the president trying to convey a kind of business-as-usual attitude, even as we're hurtling toward something very different from the ordinary Supreme Court nomination.
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管我们正飞速冲向一场与寻常最高法院提名截然不同的事件，总统却试图传达一种“一切照旧”的态度。

sentences.en: And there is no one better to do that than Amy Coney Barrett.
sentences.zh: 而没有人比艾米·科尼·巴雷特更适合担任这一角色了。

sentences.en: Thank you very much, Mr. President.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢，总统先生。

sentences.en: So President Trump introduces his nominee, Judge Amy Coney Barrett, and her husband and her seven children.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统介绍了他的提名人艾米·科尼·巴雷特法官，以及她的丈夫和七个孩子。

sentences.en: Emma, Vivian, Tess, John Peter, Liam, Juliet, and Benjamin.
sentences.zh: 艾玛、薇薇安、苔丝、约翰·彼得、利亚姆、朱丽叶和本杰明。

sentences.en: Two of the children are adopted from Haiti.
sentences.zh: 其中两个孩子是从海地领养的。

sentences.en: One has special needs.
sentences.zh: 有一个孩子有特殊需求。

sentences.en: And that was a charming tableau at the White House and a reminder in part that Judge Barrett is only 48.
sentences.zh: 那是白宫里一幅迷人的画面，也提醒人们巴雷特法官年仅48岁。

sentences.en: And if confirmed, she'd be the youngest Supreme Court justice.
sentences.zh: 如果获得确认，她将成为最年轻的最高法院大法官。

sentences.en: Should I be confirmed, I will be mindful of who came before me.
sentences.zh: 如果我获得确认，我会铭记在我之前的人。

sentences.en: She talked about Justice Ginsburg.
sentences.zh: 她谈到了金斯伯格大法官。

sentences.en: Particularly poignant to me was her long and deep friendship with Justice Antonin Scalia, my own mentor.
sentences.zh: 对我而言，特别感人的是她与我的导师安东宁·斯卡利亚大法官之间深厚的友谊。

sentences.en: She talked about the friendship between Justice Ginsburg and Justice Antonin
sentences.zh: 她谈到了金斯伯格大法官与安东宁·

sentences.en: Scalia, for whom Judge Barrett had clerked.
sentences.zh: 斯卡利亚大法官之间的友谊，巴雷特法官曾担任过斯卡利亚的书记员。

sentences.en: These two great Americans demonstrated that arguments, even about matters of great consequence, need not destroy affection.
sentences.zh: 这两位伟大的美国人证明了，即使在重大问题上的争论，也不必破坏彼此的情谊。

sentences.en: And Judge Barrett wrapped up by saying that she wanted to be a justice for all of the American people.
sentences.zh: 巴雷特法官最后表示，她希望成为所有美国人民的大法官。

sentences.en: If confirmed, I would not assume that role for the sake of those in my own circle, and certainly not for my own sake.
sentences.zh: 如果获得确认，我不会为了我圈子里的人，当然更不会为了我自己的利益而担任这一角色。

sentences.en: I would assume this role to serve you and faithfully and impartially discharge my duties under the United States Constitution.
sentences.zh: 我担任这一角色是为了服务于你们，并忠实、公正地履行我在美国宪法下的职责。

sentences.en: Well, let's talk about what we do know about the kind of justice that Judge Amy Coney Barrett would be.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们谈谈我们所了解的艾米·科尼·巴雷特法官会是怎样的一位大法官。

sentences.en: Tell us her story.
sentences.zh: 讲讲她的故事吧。

sentences.en: So she was born and raised in New Orleans in a religious Catholic family, attended Rhodes College and Notre Dame Law School, had a stellar academic record.
sentences.zh: 她出生并成长于新奥尔良的一个虔诚天主教家庭，就读于罗兹学院和圣母大学法学院，拥有出色的学术记录。

sentences.en: And although Notre Dame is not typically a feeder into judicial clerkships, she got a very high-profile judicial clerkship on the D.C.
sentences.zh: 虽然圣母大学通常不是司法书记员的输送学校，但她获得了一个备受瞩目的司法书记员职位，是在华盛顿的联邦上诉法院——

sentences.en: Circuit, the Federal Appeals Court in Washington.
sentences.zh: 哥伦比亚特区巡回上诉法院。

sentences.en: And it was after that clerkship on the Federal Appeals Court that she made the most important professional move of her life when she was hired for that clerkship with
sentences.zh: 正是在联邦上诉法院担任书记员之后，她做出了人生中最重要的职业选择，当时她被聘为

sentences.en: Justice Scalia.
sentences.zh: 斯卡利亚大法官的书记员。

sentences.en: So she's now working at the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 所以她现在在最高法院工作。

sentences.en: So tell us about working for Scalia.
sentences.zh: 那么，说说为斯卡利亚工作是什么样的吧。

sentences.en: It's the most prestigious credential in American law.
sentences.zh: 这是美国法律界最负盛名的资历。

sentences.en: Justice Scalia was a giant of conservative jurisprudence.
sentences.zh: 斯卡利亚大法官是保守派法理学的泰斗。

sentences.en: He worked closely with his four law clerks, but everyone said Amy Coney was his favorite.
sentences.zh: 他与四位法律书记员工作密切，但大家都说艾米·科尼是他最器重的一位。

sentences.en: And she then and now adopted his jurisprudential philosophies, ones that generally lead to conservative results and ones that were pioneered by Justice Scalia.
sentences.zh: 她当时和现在都采纳了他的法理哲学，这些哲学通常导致保守的结果，并且是由斯卡利亚大法官开创的。

sentences.en: What do you mean, pioneered?
sentences.zh: 你说的“开创”是什么意思？

sentences.en: My fellow Americans, I've said on several occasions that I wouldn't comment about the...
sentences.zh: 我亲爱的美国同胞们，我曾多次说过，我不会评论关于……

sentences.en: Well, the conservative legal movement in the Reagan administration in the 80s was very frustrated by what it saw as the excesses of the Warren Court.
sentences.zh: 80年代里根政府时期的保守派法律运动，对沃伦法院所表现出的过度行为感到非常沮丧。

sentences.en: For my entire political life, I've spoken about the need for the Supreme Court to interpret the law, not make it.
sentences.zh: 在我整个政治生涯中，我一直强调最高法院需要解释法律，而不是制定法律。

sentences.en: In taking what they said was a kind of freewheeling attitude toward the Constitution and finding or inventing rights in the Constitution for criminal defendants, for abortion.
sentences.zh: 他们对宪法采取了一种随心所欲的态度，为刑事被告和堕胎问题在宪法中寻找或发明权利。

sentences.en: Too many theorists believe that the courts should save the country from the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 太多的理论家认为法院应该从宪法手中拯救国家。

sentences.en: But I believe it's time to save the Constitution from them.
sentences.zh: 但我认为现在是时候从他们手中拯救宪法了。

sentences.en: And they needed a theory to constrain judges.
sentences.zh: 他们需要一种理论来约束法官。

sentences.en: During my presidency, I've proudly appointed two new justices who understand that important principle.
sentences.zh: 在我的总统任期内，我自豪地任命了两位理解这一重要原则的新大法官。

sentences.en: Justice Sandra Day O'Connor and Justice Antonin Scalia.
sentences.zh: 桑德拉·戴·奥康纳大法官和安东宁·斯卡利亚大法官。

sentences.en: And the theory has two basic prongs.
sentences.zh: 这一理论有两个基本支柱。

sentences.en: I am one of a small but hearty breed of interpretists left in the world who are called textualists or originalists.
sentences.zh: 我是世界上仅存的少数坚定的解释主义者之一，被称为文本主义者或原旨主义者。

sentences.en: One is textualism, which is about federal statutes and means to read federal statutes according to their plain words.
sentences.zh: 一是文本主义，涉及联邦法规，意味着根据联邦法规的字面意思来解读它们。

sentences.en: People ask me, why?
sentences.zh: 人们问我，为什么？

sentences.en: When did you become a textualist?
sentences.zh: 你是什么时候成为文本主义者的？

sentences.en: What caused you to become a textualist?
sentences.zh: 是什么让你成为文本主义者的？

sentences.en: You know, when did you begin eating human beings?
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像问你什么时候开始吃人一样？

sentences.en: You know, as though it's some weird thing, you know?
sentences.zh: 你知道，就好像那是什么奇怪的事情一样，明白吗？

sentences.en: I mean, when did you begin to become not a textualist?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你什么时候开始不再是文本主义者的？

sentences.en: You have a text.
sentences.zh: 你手里有文本。

sentences.en: You should read the text.
sentences.zh: 你应该阅读文本。

sentences.en: And then when you move to the Constitution, the restraining theory was called originalism.
sentences.zh: 然后当你转向宪法时，这种约束理论被称为原旨主义。

sentences.en: And originalism means to recover the original meaning of the Constitution as understood by the people who drafted and ratified it.
sentences.zh: 原旨主义意味着恢复宪法在起草和批准它的人们所理解的原始含义。

sentences.en: We try to figure out what it meant when it was adopted.
sentences.zh: 我们试图弄清楚它在被采纳时意味着什么。

sentences.en: And there, too, Scalia would say, if the Constitution doesn't speak to an issue, judges aren't meant to interpret it to find rights that didn't exist there.
sentences.zh: 同样，斯卡利亚会说，如果宪法没有涉及某个问题，法官就不应该去解释它以寻找原本不存在的权利。

sentences.en: And the Warren Court had gone astray, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说，沃伦法院已经误入歧途了。

sentences.en: You want a right to an abortion?
sentences.zh: 你想要堕胎权？

sentences.en: It's in there.
sentences.zh: 宪法里有。

sentences.en: You want a right to die?
sentences.zh: 你想要死亡权？

sentences.en: It's in there.
sentences.zh: 宪法里有。

sentences.en: Whatever is good and true and beautiful, never mind the text.
sentences.zh: 无论什么是美好、真实和美丽的，别管文本怎么说。

sentences.en: It's irrelevant.
sentences.zh: 那无关紧要。

sentences.en: He would say the same thing about finding a right to same-sex marriage.
sentences.zh: 他对于寻找同性婚姻权利也会说同样的话。

sentences.en: He would say those are not things for judges to decide.
sentences.zh: 他会说那些不是法官应该决定的事情。

sentences.en: Those are things for, in a democracy, the people to decide through their state legislatures.
sentences.zh: 在民主制度下，那些是应该由人民通过州立法机构来决定的事情。

sentences.en: But his rationale for that was democracy, that this is the enacted text.
sentences.zh: 但他对此的理由是民主，即这是已颁布的文本。

sentences.en: It went through the process of ratification or a constitutional amendment to become a law.
sentences.zh: 它经过了批准程序或宪法修正案才成为法律。

sentences.en: And if we change the law now to comport with our current understandings or what we want it to mean, then it ceased to be the law that has democratic legitimacy.
sentences.zh: 如果我们现在为了符合我们当前的理解或我们希望它意味着什么而改变法律，那么它就不再是具有民主合法性的法律了。

sentences.en: So as a student and a disciple of Scalia's, Amy Coney Barrett is identified with this judicial approach, textualism, originalism.
sentences.zh: 因此，作为斯卡利亚的学生和追随者，艾米·科尼·巴雷特被认为认同这种司法方法：文本主义和原旨主义。

sentences.en: Very much so.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And she talks about it at great length in her writings, in her judicial opinions, and in her public appearances.
sentences.zh: 她在自己的著作、司法意见书和公开露面中对此进行了详尽的阐述。

sentences.en: So Justice Scalia resisted the notion that the Supreme Court should be in the business of imposing its views of social mores on the American people.
sentences.zh: 斯卡利亚大法官抵制那种认为最高法院应该将自己的社会习俗观点强加给美国人民的观念。

sentences.en: He thought that things that the Constitution didn't declare off-limits were up to the people to decide.
sentences.zh: 他认为宪法没有宣布为禁区的事情，应该由人民自己决定。

sentences.en: And so how do we see this play out in Amy Coney Barrett's career?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们如何在艾米·科尼·巴雷特的职业生涯中看到这一点？

sentences.en: After the clerkship, she briefly practices at a prestigious Washington law firm.
sentences.zh: 在担任书记员之后，她在华盛顿一家著名的律师事务所短暂执业。

sentences.en: But she fairly quickly goes back to Notre Dame, where she's a professor and a distinguished one, beloved by her students, winning all sorts of awards.
sentences.zh: 但她很快就回到了圣母大学，在那里担任教授，是一位深受学生爱戴、屡获殊荣的杰出学者。

sentences.en: And where she continues to work on these projects about the nature of originalism, the connection between originalism and precedent.
sentences.zh: 在那里，她继续从事关于原旨主义本质、原旨主义与先例之间联系的项目研究。

sentences.en: And she comes to the attention of conservative legal groups, notably the Federalist Society, and to the Trump White House.
sentences.zh: 她引起了保守派法律团体（特别是联邦党人学会）以及特朗普白宫的注意。

sentences.en: And in 2017, President Trump nominates her to the Federal Appeals Court in Chicago,
sentences.zh: 2017年，特朗普总统提名她进入芝加哥的联邦上诉法院，

sentences.en: the United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit, where she has now participated in hundreds of decisions.
sentences.zh: 即美国第七巡回上诉法院，她现在已经参与了数百项裁决。

sentences.en: So I want to come back to this work that she did on the connection between originalism and precedent.
sentences.zh: 我想回到她关于原旨主义与先例之间联系的研究工作。

sentences.en: But first, tell us about a case that she was involved in on the Federal Court, on the Seventh Circuit, that helps us understand how she applies Justice Scalia's philosophy.
sentences.zh: 但首先，请告诉我们她参与过的一起联邦法院（第七巡回法院）案件，这有助于我们理解她如何应用斯卡利亚大法官的哲学。

sentences.en: So a case that jumped out at me was one in which she dissented.
sentences.zh: 有一个案件引起了我的注意，她在该案中投了反对票。

sentences.en: It involved a guy named Ricky Cantor, who got himself in some trouble for Medicaid fraud.
sentences.zh: 案件涉及一个名叫里基·坎特的人，他因医疗补助欺诈惹上了麻烦。

sentences.en: He apparently was billing for shoe inserts that he wasn't supposed to be billing for.
sentences.zh: 他显然在为不该报销的鞋垫进行报销申报。

sentences.en: And he's convicted of a felony, goes on to lead a blameless life, and wants to get a gun.
sentences.zh: 他被判犯有重罪，之后过着清白的生活，并想获得持枪权。

sentences.en: But there's a federal law and a Wisconsin law that says former felons are not allowed to carry guns.
sentences.zh: 但联邦法律和威斯康星州法律规定，前重罪犯不得携带枪支。

sentences.en: And he challenges these laws.
sentences.zh: 他挑战了这些法律。

sentences.en: And the court on which Judge Barrett sits, two to one, says the laws are fine.
sentences.zh: 巴雷特法官所在的法院以二比一的投票结果裁定这些法律没问题。

sentences.en: The laws do not offend the Second Amendment.
sentences.zh: 这些法律并未违反第二修正案。

sentences.en: Judge Barrett decides she's going to have a hard look at the historical evidence.
sentences.zh: 巴雷特法官决定仔细审视历史证据。

sentences.en: And she and her law clerks do what critics might call law office history.
sentences.zh: 她和她的书记员们做了批评者可能称之为“律师事务所历史研究”的事情。

sentences.en: Real historians aren't particularly crazy about judges doing history.
sentences.zh: 真正的历史学家并不太喜欢法官去搞历史研究。

sentences.en: And comes to the conclusion that the founding generation had views about this and would allow restrictions, but only for violent felonies.
sentences.zh: 她得出的结论是，建国一代对此有看法，并且会允许限制，但仅限于暴力重罪。

sentences.en: Therefore, she would have allowed this guy to get a gun.
sentences.zh: 因此，她本会允许这个人获得枪支。

sentences.en: And what's interesting about it is not so much the result, but her commitment to the methodology
sentences.zh: 这个案件有趣的地方不在于结果，而在于她致力于这种方法论，

sentences.en: of trying to unearth what is surely a difficult task of what was the view at the time about nonviolent felonies like Medicaid fraud in, you know, a generation that would have

sentences.en: So Adam, let's turn to the next couple of weeks and what it might mean to have Judge
sentences.zh: 那么亚当，让我们谈谈接下来的几周，以及艾米·科尼·巴雷特法官进入最高法院意味着什么。

sentences.en: Amy Coney Barrett on the high court.
sentences.zh: 艾米·科尼·巴雷特进入最高法院。

sentences.en: And just to get this out of the way, is there any reason to believe that she will not be confirmed?
sentences.zh: 为了先解决这个问题，有什么理由认为她不会获得确认吗？

sentences.en: There's no reason to think she's not going to make it.
sentences.zh: 没有理由认为她无法通过。

sentences.en: I mean, something could come up, but at the moment, the Republicans have the votes and the timetable looks like she can be confirmed before the election.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，可能会出现变数，但目前共和党人掌握了选票，时间表显示她可以在大选前获得确认。

sentences.en: Okay, so what will that mean for the makeup and the dynamics of the Supreme Court?
sentences.zh: 好的，那么这对最高法院的构成和动态意味着什么？

sentences.en: So there's two ways to think about it, Michael.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，可以从两个方面来思考这个问题。

sentences.en: The first one is a little simpler, and that is if you put Judge Barrett on the ideological array on the court.
sentences.zh: 第一种方式比较简单，就是把巴雷特法官放在法院的意识形态阵列中来看。

sentences.en: You can imagine the court from left to right, from Sotomayor on the left to Thomas on the right.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象一下法院从左到右的排列，从左翼的索托马约尔到右翼的托马斯。

sentences.en: You plop her in, she's probably to the right of Gorsuch and Kavanaugh, and that makes Justice
sentences.zh: 如果你把她放进去，她可能在戈萨奇和卡瓦诺的右侧，这使得卡瓦诺大法官，而不是罗伯茨首席大法官，成为法院意识形态中心的人物，在某些情况下，他可能会成为摇摆票。

sentences.en: Kavanaugh, rather than Chief Justice Roberts, the justice at the ideological center of the court and who might be in some situations the swing justice on the court.
sentences.zh: 卡瓦诺大法官，而不是罗伯茨首席大法官，成为法院意识形态中心的人物，在某些情况下，他可能会成为摇摆票。

sentences.en: Under this simple-minded theory, it moves the court slightly to the right.
sentences.zh: 按照这种简单的理论，法院会向右微倾。

sentences.en: But there's a second way to think about it, which is that it's a dynamic process, and the
sentences.zh: 但还有第二种思考方式，即这是一个动态过程，首席大法官不会轻易放弃他塑造法院的能力。

sentences.en: Chief Justice is not going to lightly give up his ability to shape the court.
sentences.zh: 首席大法官不会轻易放弃他塑造法院的能力。

sentences.en: And Chief Justice Roberts, as a consequence, although he has occasionally, and I stress very
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管罗伯茨首席大法官偶尔——我强调是非常偶尔——加入四人自由派阵营，为自由派的结果创造多数票，但他无法再与仅剩三人的自由派阵营做到这一点了。

sentences.en: occasionally, joined what was a four-member liberal wing to create a majority for a liberal result, he can't do that anymore with a three-member liberal wing.

sentences.en: If he goes with the three-member liberal wing, he will be in dissent in a 5-4 decision.
sentences.zh: 如果他与三名自由派大法官站在一起，他将在5比4的裁决中成为少数派。

sentences.en: That's not going to be attractive to him.
sentences.zh: 这对他是没有吸引力的。

sentences.en: More attractive to him is to stay with his usual allies, where he can use his distinctive power as Chief Justice to shape, maybe moderate, the results.
sentences.zh: 对他而言，更有吸引力的是与他通常的盟友保持一致，这样他就能利用自己作为首席大法官的独特权力来塑造，甚至缓和裁决结果。

sentences.en: So there's some reason to think, some substantial reason to think, that adding Judge Barrett to the court will shift the Chief Justice slightly to the right.

sentences.en: So you're saying the Chief Justice will be less inclined to side with and work with the liberal justices, because mathematically, the question becomes, what's the point?

sentences.en: But where does that leave the Chief Justice's determination, which you have described many times on the show, to have the Supreme Court be seen as an apolitical body by using his
sentences.zh: 但你曾在节目中多次提到，首席大法官决心通过利用他的投票来左右整个法院，从而使最高法院被视为一个非政治性机构，那么他的这种决心又将何去何从？

sentences.en: vote to sway the whole court?
sentences.zh: 投票来左右整个法院？

sentences.en: It would seem like he would inevitably have to kind of cede that role.
sentences.zh: 看起来他将不可避免地不得不放弃那种角色。

sentences.en: Yeah, it would withdraw a tool from his toolbox, and that will be frustrating to him.

sentences.en: If he wants to single-handedly show that the court is nonpartisan, apolitical, it's going to be harder for him to do that in this new configuration.
sentences.zh: 如果他想凭一己之力证明法院是非党派、非政治性的，那么在这种新的格局下，他将更难做到这一点。

sentences.en: Well, then let's talk about the issues that are most top of mind for Americans when it comes to what it will mean to have Amy Coney Barrett sitting on the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们谈谈美国人最关心的议题，即艾米·科尼·巴雷特进入最高法院意味着什么。

sentences.zh: 那我们先从堕胎问题开始，当然。

sentences.zh: 你能告诉我们什么，能帮助我们理解她进入法院后会发生什么吗？

sentences.en: President Trump has vowed to put justices on the court who will overrule Roe.

sentences.en: Wade.
sentences.zh: 韦德案”。

sentences.en: Would you agree with me that it would have a massive disruptive effect on the lives of countless Americans?
sentences.zh: 你是否同意我的观点，即这对无数美国人的生活将产生巨大的破坏性影响？

sentences.en: Well, Senator, I don't think I ought to express personal opinions for the reason why nominees have drawn that, for the same reason that nominees have given in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，参议员，我认为我不应该表达个人观点，原因和过去被提名人给出的理由一样。

sentences.en: Though she hasn't directly said in public that she wants to overrule Roe.
sentences.zh: 虽然她没有在公开场合直接说她想推翻“罗诉韦德案”。

sentences.en: And it's clearly binding on all courts of appeals.

sentences.en: And so it's not open to me or up to me.
sentences.zh: 所以这对我来说不是开放的，也不是我能决定的。

sentences.en: And I would have no interest in, as a court of appeals judge, challenging that precedent.
sentences.zh: 作为一名上诉法院法官，我没有兴趣去挑战这一先例。

sentences.en: It would bind.
sentences.zh: 它具有约束力。

sentences.en: If it's true that she thinks, as Justice Scalia does, that the Constitution has nothing to say about abortion,
sentences.zh: 如果她像斯卡利亚大法官那样认为宪法对堕胎只字未提，这是真的的话，

sentences.en: the question you're left with is, does she think it's the sort of precedent that should not be overruled, even if she thinks it's wrong, which she almost surely does?
sentences.zh: 你留下的问题是，她是否认为这是一种不应该被推翻的先例，即使她认为它是错误的——而她几乎肯定认为是错误的？

sentences.en: And there she's done some writing, which suggests, at least, that in the hierarchy of precedents, which are more open to being overruled than others,
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，她写过一些文章，至少暗示了在先例的等级制度中，有些先例比其他先例更容易被推翻，

sentences.en: Roe is among those that's more open to be overruled because it's been so controversial for so long.
sentences.zh: “罗诉韦德案”属于那些更容易被推翻的先例，因为它长期以来一直备受争议。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this brings us back to you telling us that at Notre Dame,
sentences.zh: 这让我们回到你之前告诉我们的，在圣母大学时，

sentences.zh: 艾米·科尼·巴雷特曾撰文探讨原旨主义与先例之间的关系。

sentences.en: Are you saying that what you just described is her view of that relationship, that there's a kind of hierarchy involved that makes some big cases more open to overruling?
sentences.zh: 你是说你刚才描述的就是她对这种关系的看法吗？即存在一种等级制度，使得一些重大案件更容易被推翻？

sentences.en: Yes, I do think that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我确实这么认为。

sentences.en: I think that she thinks that the Constitution is more important than judicial decisions.
sentences.zh: 我认为她认为宪法比司法判决更重要。

sentences.en: And I also think that she thinks that some precedents are less worthy of respect than others and that Roe falls into the less worthy of respect category.
sentences.zh: 我也认为她认为某些先例不如其他先例值得尊重，而“罗诉韦德案”属于不那么值得尊重的类别。

sentences.en: So for the many, many people for whom I imagine this will be the most pressing question on their minds, and with this nominee,
sentences.zh: 所以，对于许多许多人来说，我想这将是他们心中最紧迫的问题，而对于这位被提名人，

sentences.en: are you expecting that Roe v.

sentences.en: Wade will be challenged in the near future, a future where presumably Amy Coney Barrett is on the bench?
sentences.zh: 韦德案”在不久的将来会受到挑战，在一个艾米·科尼·巴雷特大概率已经在席上的未来？

sentences.zh: 如果是这样，你是否预计巴雷特会投票推翻它？

sentences.en: I think the day will come, but not particularly soon, when the court is asked to confront the question of overruling Roe.
sentences.zh: 我认为那一天会到来，但不会特别快，届时法院将被要求面对推翻“罗诉韦德案”的问题。

sentences.en: In the short term, I think the court is more likely to restrict and chip away at and hollow out the right to abortion and make it harder for women in red states to get abortions.

sentences.en: Should the day come when the question is squarely posed to the court, and I think Chief Justice Roberts will do what he can to push that day back?
sentences.zh: 如果有一天法院直接面对这个问题，我想罗伯茨首席大法官会尽其所能推迟那一天吗？

sentences.en: I'd be very surprised if she did not vote to overrule Roe.
sentences.zh: 如果她不投票推翻“罗诉韦德案”，我会感到非常惊讶。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.zh: 亚当，我认为人们关心的下一个大问题是《平价医疗法案》，法院目前已经受理了相关案件。

sentences.en: And I know that that case involves the constitutionality of the individual mandate.
sentences.zh: 我知道该案涉及个人强制保险条款的合宪性。

sentences.en: What can we expect there with an Amy Coney Barrett as justice?
sentences.zh: 如果艾米·科尼·巴雷特担任大法官，我们对此有何期待？

sentences.en: Yeah, so that case will be argued a week after Election Day.
sentences.zh: 是的，该案将在大选后一周进行辩论。

sentences.en: If the current timetable holds, Judge Barrett will be on the court.
sentences.zh: 如果目前的时间表不变，巴雷特法官届时将会在最高法院。

sentences.en: She has been critical of the 2012 decision, which upheld the constitutionality of the individual mandate, which required people to buy insurance or pay a penalty.
sentences.zh: 她曾批评过2012年的裁决，该裁决维持了个人强制保险条款的合宪性，即要求人们购买保险或支付罚款。

sentences.en: Now, the new case involves different issues, and I don't think her vote is particularly predictable.
sentences.zh: 现在，新案件涉及不同的问题，我不认为她的投票特别可预测。

sentences.en: And I don't think the court's outcome is particularly predictable.
sentences.zh: 我也不认为法院的结果特别可预测。

sentences.en: To be sure, if you still had Justice Ginsburg on the court, you would have the same five-justice coalition who saved the individual mandate in 2012.
sentences.zh: 可以肯定的是，如果金斯伯格大法官还在法院，你将拥有在2012年拯救了个人强制保险条款的那五位大法官联盟。

sentences.en: But the question in the case is convoluted enough and kind of a stretch that I don't know that you won't have a lopsided majority, even of a conservative court,
sentences.zh: 但案件中的问题足够复杂，而且有点牵强，我不知道即使在一个保守派法院中，是否会出现一边倒的多数票，

sentences.en: rejecting much of the latest challenge.
sentences.zh: 驳回大部分最新的挑战。

sentences.en: Finally, Adam, let's talk about the Supreme Court and the election itself.
sentences.zh: 最后，亚当，让我们谈谈最高法院和大选本身。

sentences.en: The president has said that if he loses in November, he may not accept the results.
sentences.zh: 总统曾表示，如果他在11月落败，他可能不会接受结果。

sentences.en: In fact, he may challenge them.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他可能会挑战结果。

sentences.en: What would it mean to find the United States in a Bush v.
sentences.zh: 如果美国陷入类似“布什诉戈尔案”的情况，最高法院被要求对2020年大选结果进行裁决，甚至可能是决定性的裁决，而此时一位上任仅几天的新大法官参与其中，

sentences.en: Gore-like situation where the Supreme Court is asked to weigh in on the results of the 2020 election, perhaps decisively, with a new justice who is literally days old in the job
sentences.zh: 布什诉戈尔案”的情况，最高法院被要求对2020年大选结果进行裁决，甚至可能是决定性的裁决，而此时一位上任仅几天的新大法官参与其中，

sentences.en: and who was rushed through by the sitting president despite lots of opposition and despite polling that shows that a majority of Americans
sentences.zh: 并且是在现任总统不顾大量反对，也不顾民调显示大多数美国人认为不应该在这个时间表上进行的情况下强行推进的，这会意味着什么？

sentences.en: didn't think it should have happened on this timetable?
sentences.zh: 认为不应该在这个时间表上进行的情况下强行推进的，这会意味着什么？

sentences.en: So we don't know what the case would look like, what the legal issues would be.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不知道案件会是什么样子，法律问题会是什么。

sentences.en: They could come from anywhere in the nation.
sentences.zh: 它们可能来自全国任何地方。

sentences.en: But I agree with you, Michael, that some election-related case is sadly likely to reach the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 但我同意你的看法，迈克尔，一些与选举相关的案件很遗憾可能会到达最高法院。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Here, I think most of the justices will join Chief Justice Roberts in really wanting to maintain the legitimacy of the Supreme Court and not hand a victory for political reasons
sentences.zh: 在这里，我认为大多数大法官会加入罗伯茨首席大法官的行列，真正希望维护最高法院的合法性，而不是因为政治原因将胜利拱手让给特朗普总统，

sentences.en: to President Trump, who had just appointed a third justice to the court.
sentences.zh: 他刚刚任命了第三位大法官进入法院。

sentences.en: So I think all Americans can be hopeful and the Supreme Court will try hard that that case, when it arises, will be decided on strictly legal grounds.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为所有美国人都可以抱有希望，最高法院会努力确保该案在出现时，能严格在法律基础上作出裁决。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: But what you're saying is it's very conceivable
sentences.zh: 但你的意思是，完全可以想象，

sentences.en: that a justice just appointed by this president may be asked to vote as a justice on a case that could determine whether or not he stays president.
sentences.zh: 一位刚由这位总统任命的大法官，可能会被要求对一个可能决定他是否能继续担任总统的案件进行投票。

sentences.en: At her confirmation hearing,
sentences.zh: 在她的确认听证会上，

sentences.en: Judge Barrett is certain to be asked whether she's going to recuse herself from such a case.
sentences.zh: 巴雷特法官肯定会被问及她是否会在此类案件中回避。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: The answer will be very interesting.
sentences.zh: 答案会非常有趣。

sentences.en: I imagine she'll duck it.
sentences.zh: 我想她会回避这个问题。

sentences.en: But there would be something a little odd about someone arriving at the court in these circumstances voting in a case of that significance.
sentences.zh: 但让一个在这种情况下进入法院的人，对如此重要的案件进行投票，会显得有点奇怪。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Adam, how are you generally thinking about the historic nature of all this?
sentences.zh: 亚当，你总体上是如何看待这一切的历史意义的？

sentences.en: You are a actual lawyer.
sentences.zh: 你是一位真正的律师。

sentences.en: You're a student of the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 你是最高法院的研究者。

sentences.en: You have talked about the Warren Court, the conservative response to that, these various kind of cycles and eras in the history of the court.
sentences.zh: 你谈到过沃伦法院，谈到过对它的保守派回应，谈到过法院历史上这些不同的周期和时代。

sentences.en: What does the nomination and the likely confirmation of Amy Coney Barrett mean to you?
sentences.zh: 艾米·科尼·巴雷特的提名和可能的确认对你意味着什么？

sentences.en: I think it's terrible for the court.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对法院来说是可怕的。

sentences.en: I think Justice Scalia's death shaped the last election and the Senate Republicans' refusal to even hold hearings for President Obama's nominee,
sentences.zh: 我认为斯卡利亚大法官的去世影响了上次大选，而参议院共和党人拒绝为奥巴马总统的提名人梅里克·加兰举行听证会，这对法院来说是可怕的。

sentences.en: Merrick Garland, was terrible for the court.
sentences.zh: 梅里克·加兰，这对法院来说是可怕的。

sentences.en: I think this is terrible for the court.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对法院来说是可怕的。

sentences.en: It's a real argument in favor of term limits or mandatory retirements.
sentences.zh: 这是一个支持任期限制或强制退休的有力论据。

sentences.en: The fact that two elections in a row are being shaped by the untimely deaths of towering figures in American law just doesn't make any sense.
sentences.zh: 连续两次大选都受到美国法律界泰斗意外去世的影响，这根本说不通。

sentences.en: And why is that?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: Why is this so terrible for the court?
sentences.zh: 为什么这对法院来说如此可怕？

sentences.en: The court tries hard.
sentences.zh: 法院很努力。

sentences.en: Sometimes it fails.
sentences.zh: 有时它会失败。

sentences.en: But it tries hard to make legal decisions, not partisan political decisions.
sentences.zh: 但它努力做出法律决定，而不是党派政治决定。

sentences.en: And in order for it to maintain the respect of the American people, it needs to be seen that way.
sentences.zh: 为了保持美国人民的尊重，它需要被那样看待。

sentences.en: And now in the coming weeks, we are going to be told over and over again, and not without reason, that the court is a political institution because of the way the Senate
sentences.zh: 现在在接下来的几周里，我们将一次又一次地被告知，而且并非没有理由，由于参议院对待这项提名的方式，法院是一个政治机构。

sentences.en: is going to treat this nomination.
sentences.zh: 对待这项提名的方式。

sentences.en: But Adam, hasn't that ship sailed?
sentences.zh: 但亚当，那艘船不是已经开走了吗？

sentences.en: I mean, didn't that ship sail when Democrats treated Robert Bork the way they treated him?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当民主党人以那种方式对待罗伯特·博克时，那艘船不是已经开走了吗？

sentences.en: Didn't that ship sail when Clarence Thomas' hearings devolved into what they devolved into?
sentences.zh: 当克拉伦斯·托马斯的听证会演变成那种样子时，那艘船不是已经开走了吗？

sentences.en: Didn't that ship sail within the past few years when the Senate wouldn't even hear, as you said, a Democratic president's nominee?
sentences.zh: 在过去几年里，当参议院甚至不愿听取你所说的民主党总统的提名人时，那艘船不是已经开走了吗？

sentences.en: I mean, we've talked about this in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们过去谈过这个问题。

sentences.en: The court has become a politicized body despite its best intentions.
sentences.zh: 尽管法院有最好的初衷，但它已经变成了一个政治化的机构。

sentences.en: So is this just not the kind of logical conclusion of all that?
sentences.zh: 所以这难道不是这一切的逻辑结论吗？

sentences.en: I guess you're right, Michael.
sentences.zh: 我想你是对的，迈克尔。

sentences.en: But only months ago at the end of the last term where the court did seem to have found its way into a balanced approach to many kinds of cases and its public approval ratings
sentences.zh: 但就在几个月前，在上届任期结束时，法院似乎确实找到了一种平衡处理多种案件的方法，其公众支持率也因此上升，并且在残酷的卡瓦诺听证会之后，它试图收回部分合法性。

sentences.en: went up as a consequence and it tried to reclaim some of its legitimacy in the aftermath of the brutal Kavanaugh hearings.
sentences.zh: 其公众支持率也因此上升，并且在残酷的卡瓦诺听证会之后，它试图收回部分合法性。

sentences.en: It may be that this is just another one of a series of blows to the court.
sentences.zh: 这可能只是法院遭受的一系列打击中的又一次。

sentences.en: But this close to an election in the face of what many people describe as rank hypocrisy among Republicans who took the opposite approach four years ago, it's just not good
sentences.zh: 但在大选临近之际，面对许多人所描述的共和党人的彻底虚伪——他们四年前采取了完全相反的做法——这对法院来说确实不是好事。

sentences.en: for the court.
sentences.zh: 对法院来说。

sentences.en: A provocative question, but should Amy Coney Barrett, should the court, ask that we respect the majority of Americans and wait for the next president to proceed with this process?
sentences.zh: 一个挑衅性的问题，但艾米·科尼·巴雷特，法院是否应该要求我们尊重大多数美国人，并等待下一任总统来推进这一进程？

sentences.en: I don't think they're capable of doing that.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他们有能力做到这一点。

sentences.en: And I'm not sure that that itself doesn't have a political valence.
sentences.zh: 而且我不确定这本身是否不具有政治倾向。

sentences.en: Judge Barrett will be asked
sentences.zh: 巴雷特法官会被问及

sentences.en: how she feels about the rush
sentences.zh: 她对这种仓促行事有何感想，

sentences.en: and I imagine she'll say, that's not my job.
sentences.zh: 我想她会说，那不是我的工作。

sentences.en: That's your job, Senate.
sentences.zh: 那是你们的工作，参议院。

sentences.en: You guys are in charge of the politics.
sentences.zh: 你们负责政治。

sentences.en: I'm in charge of the law.
sentences.zh: 我负责法律。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: You all have gotten us to where this all is.
sentences.zh: 是你们把我们带到了今天这个地步。

sentences.en: It's your problem.
sentences.zh: 这是你们的问题。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Well, Adam, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，亚当，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Over the weekend, the chairman of the Senate Judiciary Committee,
sentences.zh: 周末期间，参议院司法委员会主席，

sentences.en: Lindsey Graham, said that confirmation hearings for Amy Coney Barrett will begin on October 12th.
sentences.zh: 林赛·格雷厄姆表示，艾米·科尼·巴雷特的确认听证会将于10月12日开始。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: A Times investigation based on tax return data for the president and his businesses over two decades found that he paid just $750 in federal income taxes during the year
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》基于总统及其名下企业过去二十年的纳税申报数据进行了一项调查，发现他在赢得总统大选的那一年只缴纳了750美元的联邦所得税，

sentences.en: that he won the presidency and the same amount during his first year in the White House.
sentences.zh: 在入主白宫的第一年缴纳的金额也是如此。

sentences.en: The president, who has broken tradition and refused to disclose his taxes, paid no federal income tax in 10 of the past 15 years, mostly because his businesses
sentences.zh: 这位打破传统、拒绝公开纳税情况的总统，在过去15年里有10年没有缴纳联邦所得税，这主要是因为他的企业

sentences.en: reported losing more money than they made.
sentences.zh: 申报的亏损额超过了盈利额。

sentences.en: On the New York Times story, though, you have to understand that when Americans read that you may have paid only a few hundred dollars in federal income tax per year,
sentences.zh: 不过，关于《纽约时报》的这篇报道，你必须明白，当美国人读到你每年可能只缴纳了几百美元的联邦所得税时，

sentences.en: that seems very low for someone who's a billionaire.
sentences.zh: 对于一个亿万富翁来说，这看起来太少了。

sentences.en: So how much, I mean,
sentences.zh: 那么到底是多少，我是说，

sentences.en: Well, basically, they're saying I paid nothing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，基本上，他们是在说我什么都没交。

sentences.en: Can you give people an idea of how much you actually are paying?
sentences.zh: 你能让大家了解一下你实际上缴纳了多少吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, basically, well, first of all, I paid a lot and I paid a lot of state income taxes, too.
sentences.zh: 是的，基本上，首先，我交了很多，而且我也缴纳了大量的州所得税。

sentences.en: The New York state charges a lot and I paid a lot of money in state.
sentences.zh: 纽约州收费很高，我缴纳了很大一笔州税。

sentences.en: During a news conference on Sunday night held minutes after the Times published its investigation, the president called the investigation fake news but did not take issue
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》发表调查报告几分钟后举行的周日晚间新闻发布会上，总统称该调查是假新闻，但并未对

sentences.en: with any specific details.
sentences.zh: 任何具体细节提出异议。

sentences.en: On tomorrow's show,
sentences.zh: 在明天的节目中，

sentences.en: I'll speak with the reporters who obtained the president's tax debt.
sentences.zh: 我将与获取总统税务债务数据的记者进行交谈。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine until this summer
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作，直到今年夏天，

sentences.en: when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎来了一批自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场激烈、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro with me,
sentences.zh: 在我和我主持的最新一期《地铁》节目中，

sentences.en: Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 萨拉·凯尼格，讲述了人们试图维持影响力却在过程中逐渐失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》节目。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在你收听播客的任何平台订阅收听。
